data.cultural_impact: The name Avyaan holds great cultural significance in Hindu tradition. In Hindu society, knowledge is deeply respected and considered an essential aspect for personal and societal growth. By giving their child the name Avyaan, parents hope to inspire a deep thirst for learning and wisdom. They believe that their child will carry on the legacy of their ancestors by acquiring knowledge and sharing it with the world.
data.spiritual_significance: Avyaan is a name that embodies spiritual significance. In Hindu philosophy, knowledge is considered a means to attain enlightenment and liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The name Avyaan can serve as a constant reminder for the child to seek knowledge and wisdom, not just for personal gain, but as a tool for spiritual growth and self-realization. The name also symbolizes the eternal quest for truth and understanding, which is an essential aspect of spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Avyān authored the Mahabharata, an epic Sanskrit poem and one of the two major Sanskrit epics, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the story of the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and Kaurava princes, and is set in the Indian subcontinent in the 9th or 10th century BC, likely during the late Vedic period.

Avyān is also considered the author of the Ramayana, another major Sanskrit epic, but this attribution is disputed among scholars. He is mentioned in some versions of the text as a sage and poet, but there is no definitive evidence to support this claim. The Ramayana, which tells the story of prince Rama and his exile, rescue of his wife Sita, and eventual triumph over the demon king Ravana, is believed to have been written between 300 BC and 300 AD, in the period of the early Mahajanpadas and the Mauryan Empire.
